record.context_brief: dominant maps from hypersurfaces in P4
record.original_question: What is the corresponding answer for very general hypersurfaces in P^4 to the rationality questions raised in Problem 13 for very general surfaces and complete intersections?

evidence.quote: (13.4) What happens for hypersurfaces of P4?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a very general smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge 6$ (so that $X$ is a smooth projective threefold of general type whose canonical bundle is ample). Let $f\colon X\dashrightarrow Y$ be a dominant rational map onto a smooth projective threefold $Y$.

Determine whether the following analogue of the surface result holds: is it necessarily the case that either
\begin{itemize}
\item $Y$ is rational, or
\item $f$ is birational (so $Y$ is birational to $X$)?
\end{itemize}

More generally, classify the possible targets $Y$ of such dominant rational maps from a very general hypersurface $X\subset\mathbb{P}^4$ of degree $d\ge 6$, in parallel with the known result for very general surfaces $S\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ of degree $d\ge 5$ (where any dominant rational map $S\dashrightarrow Z$ to a smooth projective surface $Z$ must have $Z$ rational or be birational) and with its extension to very general complete intersection surfaces of sufficiently high multidegree.
artifact.status_search_result: For very general surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ of degree $\ge 5$, and for very general complete intersection surfaces of high enough degree, it is known (Bastianelli, Ciliberto, Lee–Pirola and others) that any dominant rational map to a smooth projective surface is either birational or has rational target. The analogous classification for very general hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^4$ (i.e. for threefolds) does not appear to have been established; recent surveys and papers on measures of irrationality and rationality of hypersurfaces continue to list the higher-dimensional case as a question without a complete answer, indicating the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: On subfields of the function field of a general surface in P^3 (Bastianelli)
status_evidence.snippet: For a very general surface of degree d>=5 in P^3, dominant rational maps to smooth surfaces are classified.
status_evidence.claim: The surface-case (d>=5 in P^3) version of Problem 13 is established.

status_evidence.title: A Primer on Measures of Irrationality (Chen–Martin)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses dominant rational maps from very general hypersurfaces and lists open extensions to higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The threefold analogue for very general hypersurfaces in P^4 is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Rationality of hypersurfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey of rationality questions for hypersurfaces; the structure of dominant rational maps from very general quintic and higher threefolds in P^4 remains an open direction.
status_evidence.claim: Status for hypersurfaces in P^4 remains open.
